newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa courts, medics fail women -- rights group.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa courts, medics fail women -- rights group.

text.p: The South African justice and medical systems were failing women who were victims of violence, Human Rights Watch Africa said on Friday.
"The police are frequently callous or disinterested in their treatment of women and the court system is little better," the London-based organisation said in a statement.

Equally alarming, the group said, was the fact that while medical evidence was crucial to investigate and prosecute rape, few medical personnel were properly trained to collect and interpret such evidence.

Human Rights Watch said that of the 27,056 rapes reported in 1993, only 8,998 were prosecuted. Of the cases brought to court 4,753 resulted in convictions, which amounts to only 17.5 percent of the total.
Since 1993 the number of rapes reported has nearly doubled to 50,481 in 1996. Of these 21,863 were prosecuted, yet only 4,100 led to a conviction -- 8.1 percent of the cases reported.
"These worsening figures demand urgent attention," the organisation said.

South Africa's cabinet on Wednesday approved ground-breaking draft legislation severely restricting access to bail by suspects accused of serious crimes, including rape. The new bail code still has to be presented to parliament.
